questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My father lives in Munich and I wanted to strengthen my relationship with him as well as my acedemic skills in German and German Law

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Due to my contacts in Munich, I easily found housing, but in general I heard from many exchange students, that it was very difficult to int any housing and the prices were very high

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Rents are high and housing is limited

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We could choose any lectures we wanted to follow, we ust had to give the professor a notice about 2 weeks before the end of the lectures (but preferablt earlier), that we were exchange students and needed an exam to proof our attendance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange office was always available, answered very fast and wes very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I could register for all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Choose the courses that are a part of the
LLM.Eur
programme, as they give extra ECTS-credits and are tailored in a way, where you do not need any prior knowledge of German law. These classes will also always offer an Exam at the end for the
LLM.Eur
students, that Erasmus students can easily attend too. In general, even though the courses are almost all in German, they have an international perspective and the lecturers are aware of many international students present.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Even though I followed LLM courses as a BA student, the courses were not at all a too high level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There are lectures and seminars, similar to UCPH. 
The main curriculum is just following the lectures, and there is almost no additional reading, which means that the workload feels much easier than at UCPH. Some classes have cases and material online, that they expect you to have read before the lecture and recomended readings, but I did not experience having to buy any mandatory books and the expected readings were very limited.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Europarecht I, Deutsches und Europäisches Wettbewerbsrecht, Aktuelle Rechtsprechung des Bundesverfassungsgerichts, Klimaklagen, and Deutschkurs für Studierende der Rechtwissenschaften

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all the courses I took expect the German language course for law students, if the Exchange student speaks a high level of german already. The German language course was too easy. The academic courses I took were all very interesting and well tailored for a foreign student, who speaks german.
If the student only has a beginners level of german, the German language course might be good. There were also Englich courses and courses tailored specially for Erasmus students and taught in an easy German language, and my erasmus freinds seemed satisfied with these.

questions.answer: Immatriculation Fee of 144 EUR per semester

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in the supermarket is much less expensive. Going out for dinner and beer is much less expensive than Copenhagen. Wine in bars is more expensive. Public transportation is free for students in the night hours (18:00-06:00) and in weekends. If you need it every day, you can pay an extra fee to your Immatriculation Fee and use all public transportation for free the whole semester. Otherwise tickets for public transportation is quite expensive (best solution for Danes: get a bike and use it during the day and use public transportation in the evenings when going out and during week days)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use any, but there seemed to be some interesting clubs and a lot of sports opportunities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of cheap sport opportunities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sport, especially mountain sports - go rock climbing, hiking and skiining in the Alps

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Beautiful lakes around Munich, beautiful parks and castles, the Alps. Use the Englischer Garten and Olympiapark in Munich. Go shopping, cafe drinking and out at night in Maxvorstandt and Glockenbachviertel/Gärtner Platz.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak to them during class, they are all very open towards foreigners once you approach them (like danes)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get a bike but be prepared for a different biking culture than in CPH (for better and for worse), take advantage of the cheap food (also the Mensa/student cafeteria has good and very cheap meals!) and beer, go to class with interest and dedication and enjoy the limited readings and workload next to class.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is wonderful, if you speak German well. If not, it might be dificult to fully enjoy the german culture and the classes, but then you will probably get a larger erasmus student friend group instead.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting more German friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid-19

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
